title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: Price increase (+6.2%)
drivers.evidence: Past 30% off lift was x1.24; this is a price increase, not a promotion. Higher prices reduce demand. Noise-adjusted lift from promotions is x1.4, but this is a price hike. Historical data shows no lift at higher price.

drivers.name: Store closure (Mon)
drivers.evidence: 2026-09-07 (Labor Day) had 13 units vs baseline 18.7 (x0.69). Monday closure likely reduces 1/7 of weekly sales. No direct closure data, but plausible.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 18.7. The target week has no event but a price increase to $12.03 (+6.2%) and a store closure on Monday. Price hikes reduce demand; past promotions at similar discounts (10–30%) show noise-adjusted lifts of x1.4 on average, but the most recent 30% off (2026-03-16) only lifted sales x1.24. The current price is higher than usual, and no promotion is planned. The closure of Monday reduces available sales days, likely cutting volume. The week after a promotion typically sees a dip (x0.76), but no recent promotion occurred. The classical model suggests no uplift, but we adjust for price and closure. Evidence is moderate: one past closure (2026-09-07, Labor Day) had 13 units, vs baseline 18.7 (x0.69). No direct closure data, but plausible drop. We shrink toward 1.0 due to limited evidence. No seasonal ramp in baseline.

brief:
PRODUCT: Cold & Flu Relief | category Health | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 12.03 (+6.2% vs regular price 11.33)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.7 | 5%-95%: 4.5 - 37.5 | 10%-90%: 8.2 - 33.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
